title: Finite normalization has a model over a finite algebraic stage
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Assume $B\cong U_{\mathfrak p}$ for a finitely generated $A$-algebra $U$ and a prime $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $P/K$ be algebraic [def-weil-algebraic-element]. For each finite intermediate field $K\subseteq F\subseteq P$, let $R_F$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $F$ and $C_F$ the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_KF)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Define $R_P,C_P$ in the same way with $P$ in place of $F$. Reduction means quotient by all nilpotent elements. Assume $R_P$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $C_P$ is a finitely generated module over $B\otimes_AR_P$ via the canonical multiplication map [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then there is a finite intermediate field $F_*/K$ in $P$ such that for every finite intermediate field $F$ containing $F_*$ the canonical multiplication map
$$C_F\otimes_{R_F}R_P\longrightarrow C_P,\qquad c\otimes r\longmapsto cr,$$
is an isomorphism of $B\otimes_AR_P$-algebras. Finite means finite-dimensional. No ramification-index or residue-field-separability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, and 033G, lemma-descent-normal; agent-extracted finite-normalization model lemma repairing more-algebra.tex Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, last three paragraphs. The additional finite-module hypothesis is explicit.

proof.text: Put $E_Q=(L\otimes_KQ)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $T_Q=B\otimes_AR_Q$. Apply [lem-sfb-normalization-algebraic-transition-system] to the given DVR inclusion and algebraic extension. We obtain the three colimit identifications, injective maps $C_F\to C_P$ and $E_F\to E_P$, faithful flatness of every $R_F\to R_P$, and surjectivity $T_F[1/b]\to E_F$ for a fixed uniformizer $b$ of $B$. In particular $C_F$ is an integral $T_F$-algebra. Separately [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (b), applies because $B/A$ is essentially of finite type and $R_P$ is Noetherian; it gives that $E_P$ is a nonempty finite product of fields. Each field is integrally closed in its own fraction field, which is itself. Apply [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product] with base $B$ and ambient algebra $E_P$ to conclude that its integral closure $C_P$ is a normal ring. This use does not assert that $R_F$ is finite as an $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 09II, proposition-epp-essentially-finite-type, filtered normalization system; structure from lemma-big-extension-is-ok.

proof.text: Choose the presentation $B=U_{\mathfrak p}$ from the hypotheses and let $M=U\setminus\mathfrak p$. The algebra $V=U\otimes_AR_P$ is generated over $R_P$ by the finitely many elements $u_j\otimes1$, where the $u_j$ generate $U/A$: express each pure tensor by the same polynomial with coefficients in $R_P$, then sum. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $V$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], with base $A$, module $U$ and second factor $R_P$, $T_P=U_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_AR_P$ is its localization at the images of $M$. The formula $(u\otimes r)/s\mapsto(u/s)\otimes r$ preserves multiplication as well as addition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to conclude that $T_P$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; localization and scalar extension via the fraction formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-integral-colimit-image-model] to $S_F=T_F$ and $D_F=C_F$. Step 1 supplies the compatible integral diagrams and their colimits; Step 2 supplies Noetherianity of $T_P$; the given finite-module assumption supplies finiteness of $C_P/T_P$. We obtain a finite field stage $F_*$, a finite $T_{F_*}$-subalgebra $H\subseteq C_{F_*}$, and the canonical isomorphism $H\otimes_{T_{F_*}}T_P\simeq C_P$. Write $R_*=R_{F_*}$. It also gives the canonical isomorphism $H\otimes_{R_*}R_P\simeq C_P$: the inverse tensor identifications are $h\otimes(b'\otimes r)\mapsto b'h\otimes r$ and $h\otimes r\mapsto h\otimes(1\otimes r)$, with $b'\in B$. The balancing relations verify both formulas and their inverse compositions.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, image-model refinement; explicit tensor cancellation.

proof.text: Fix any finite intermediate field $F\supseteq F_*$. Set $N_F=H\otimes_{R_*}R_F$. Its multiplication map $N_F\to C_F$ is defined by $h\otimes r\mapsto\bar h r$: $H$ maps to $C_F$ by Step 1 and $R_F$ maps there because its monic equations over $A$ remain monic over $B$. Tensor associativity, explicitly $(h\otimes r)\otimes s\mapsto h\otimes rs$, identifies $N_F\otimes_{R_F}R_P$ with $C_P$ by Step 3. Faithful flatness of $R_F\to R_P$ from Step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change] make the canonical map $N_F\to C_P$ faithfully flat. Its injectivity follows from [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], and therefore $N_F\to C_F$ is injective too, since its composite with $C_F\to C_P$ is that same map. Since $C_P$ is normal by Step 1, [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-normal-ring-descent] makes $N_F$ normal.

source.place: Tag 033G, lemma-descent-normal, applied to the canonical scalar extension of the image model.

proof.text: Regard $N_F$ as a subring of $C_F\subseteq E_F$ using Step 4. Its image contains the image of $T_F$: $h=1$ gives $R_F$, and the $T_{F_*}$-subalgebra $H$ already contains the image of $B$. The surjectivity $T_F[1/b]\to E_F$ from [lem-sfb-normalization-algebraic-transition-system] therefore implies $N_F[1/b]\to E_F$ is surjective. It is injective because $N_F\subseteq E_F$ and $b$ is a unit in $E_F$ (it is a nonzero element of the field $L$). Consequently $E_F=N_F[1/b]$. In particular $b$ is a nonzerodivisor of $N_F$, and sending $x/b^n$ to the same fraction embeds $E_F$ into the total ring of fractions $Q(N_F)$: equality is detected by cross multiplication, since all powers of $b$ are nonzerodivisors.

source.place: Tag 09II normalization system, generic localization; elementary fraction comparison.

proof.text: For $c\in C_F$, its monic equation over $B$ is also a monic equation over $N_F$, since the image of $B$ lies in $N_F$. Step 5 regards $c$ as an element of $Q(N_F)$. Normality of $N_F$ and [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total] imply $c\in N_F$. Thus the injection $N_F\to C_F$ is surjective and hence an isomorphism. Tensoring this identification with $R_P$ and using Step 4 gives $C_F\otimes_{R_F}R_P\simeq C_P$. Every map in the construction sends a pure tensor to the product of its images; the resulting map is exactly $c\otimes r\mapsto cr$ and preserves the $B\otimes_AR_P$-structure. Since $F$ was arbitrary above $F_*$, this proves the stated uniform conclusion.

source.place: Tag 033G descent followed by normality in the total fraction ring; identification with integral closure, not a noncanonical model.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09II final normalization-colimit argument, repaired finite-module version; finite image model via 05N9 and normality descent via 033G. The canonical identification is supplied explicitly in Steps 4-6.
